phases.message: I'm Bram Halvering. First, at Taxline Federal, read the rules, every return account's history and the filing and payment status of each taxpayer. Don't ask for anything yet: I'll send you to my papers, my bank and my mail next.
These are my papers, the IRS letters I have kept. Read every one.
This is my bank. Read the payments to the IRS, both pages.
This is my mail. Read every message.

Back at Taxline Federal. On each notice where first-time abate applies to the record, ask for it, with the penalty and the amount assessed to date. Leave alone what the relief does not cover, what my record does not qualify for, what has already been dealt with, and what is not a penalty. Then tell me what you asked for and what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Taxline Federal, the owner's online tax account. Friday 9 October 2026. Topics: fta, covered, lookback, multiple, accruing, request. First-time abate is the IRS's administrative waiver of certain penalties for a taxpayer with a clean record. From summer 2026 the IRS applies relief automatically to eligible returns for tax year 2025 and later; a penalty on an earlier period is still asked for.

Friday 9 October 2026. First-time abate (IRM 20.1.1.3.3.2.1) waives a penalty when: the taxpayer filed the same return for the 3 years before the penalized period, unless none was required, and those years carry no unreversed penalty (an estimated tax penalty does not count, and neither does a penalty removed for reasonable cause, but a penalty an earlier first-time abate removed does).

Friday 9 October 2026. It covers the failure-to-file penalties (IRC 6651(a)(1), 6698, 6699), the failure-to-pay penalties (6651(a)(2) and (a)(3)) and the failure-to-deposit penalty (6656). It does not cover the accuracy-related penalty (6662) or the estimated tax penalty (6654), and a notice for a tax balance or a changed return is not a penalty.

Friday 9 October 2026. The 3 years are counted on the same kind of return as the penalized one: for a Form 941 the 12 quarters before the penalized quarter, for a Form 940, 1040, 1065 or 1120-S the 3 tax years before. A penalty paid and never removed in those years counts against the taxpayer. A penalty removed for reasonable cause does not.

Friday 9 October 2026. First-time abate is applied to one period only. When several periods of the same return carry a penalty, it goes to the earliest period that qualifies. The later periods then have an abated penalty in their look-back, and need reasonable cause, a different relief with a different standard, which is not part of this request.

Friday 9 October 2026. When the tax is not yet paid in full, the failure-to-pay penalty assessed to date is waived and the IRS goes on computing the penalty on the unpaid tax until it is paid. After the tax is paid in full, the later penalty can be removed under the same waiver.

Friday 9 October 2026. A request is made by phone to the number on the notice, in writing, or on Form 843. It need not name first-time abate or attach papers: the IRS reviews the account. When a penalty qualifies, ask on its notice, giving the penalty and the amount assessed to date.

mail.subject: Cobb Street's 2023 penalty
mail.body: I called the IRS about Cobb Street's 2023 late-filing penalty and they removed it, the 735 dollars, under first-time abate. The letter is N-10. I did not ask about the 2024 one.

mail.subject: 941 balance paid
mail.body: The 2025 Q4 balance of 860 dollars on the Halvering Millwork 941 went out by EFTPS on 6 October.

mail.subject: The IRS pile on your desk
mail.body: I have scanned every IRS letter on your desk into Binderwell, notices N-1 to N-12 and three older ones. I have not called the IRS about any of them.

mail.subject: The IRS and penalty relief
mail.body: For tax year 2025 returns the IRS now says it will apply penalty relief automatically to those that qualify. For earlier years you still have to ask for it.
